info.title: YSP shared transport, session and operation lookup
info.description:
Leader-authored P00 transport contract, 24 October 2026. Parent spec: https://github.com/Kamunggay/YSP/issues/2. This is a review candidate; no routes, authentication, durable operations, stock or money are implemented. Glenn's frontend/query review and Efren's posting review remain pending. PRD v1.2/TRD v2.1 retain review-candidate status.

Validate from a clean checkout: `npm --prefix contracts/transport ci --ignore-scripts` then `npm --prefix contracts/transport test`. Node 24.11.1 was used for this contract harness only; P01 selects/pins supported application runtimes separately. Tests use strict Ajv 2020-12 with date-time format assertions and a formal OpenAPI validator. examples.json contains validating expected wire examples; executed schema checks never establish business acceptance.

CommandContext is normalized adapter metadata, not an HTTP command body. Bind chapter/action to the authorized route, Idempotency-Key to the mutation header and explicit expected versions/reference to the endpoint body. Endpoint contracts supply their real domain payload and enumerate the ActionResult.data/state fields. There is no shared POST or public balance setter. Identity/record/evidence payloads are the identity, record and evidence contract, opening acceptance 02, inventory query/hold semantics 03; execution stays in Stage 1.

For eventual mutations, success uses 200/201 and action_result=success. Correctable field input uses 422/blocked; domain or changed-key conflicts use 409/blocked (an owning contract may retain its established 423 gate status). Concurrent stale row/material input uses 409/stale. Current authentication/authorization failure uses 401/403/forbidden. Unknown outcome is never fabricated as blocked or success. Lookup HTTP 200 can contain an uncertain result; inspect action_result and operation.outcome. Current authorization is checked for every lookup/replay; an old requester or public ID grants no inherited access.

Keep editable draft data separate from the immutable attempted payload, chapter, action, key, versions and known operation ID. Validation errors preserve correct input and show JSON-pointer field feedback alongside the blocking reason and permitted next action. A stale response supplies authorized current metadata for comparison without overwriting the draft or silently substituting versions. Definitive correctable rejection permits a reviewed new attempt with a new key after changed payload; never silently mutate the payload under an old key. Physical actions already performed require reconciliation even if database commitment was rejected or is unknown.

On timeout, retain that exact attempt and look up action+key in its original authorized chapter; if known, a scoped operation ID is also supported. No visible terminal row may mean the original request is still in flight. Unavailable/malformed/non-JSON lookup keeps uncertainty. Do not issue automatic new attempts, switch chapter/key to bypass uncertainty, or offer another physical handover. After a visible terminal result, only the owning operation's current policy and authorized next steps govern any new reviewed attempt. An internal deadlock retry uses the unchanged business identity/payload and never redoes physical activity.

get.summary: Look up the original action and key in an authorized chapter
get.description: Read only. Reject missing action/key, unknown or mixed query selectors. No chapter/action/key uniqueness is widened. No visible result means uncertain, including an in-flight or not-yet-visible terminal transaction.

parameters.name: chapter_id
parameters.description: Selected chapter subject to current server membership/duty authorization, never an authority grant.

200.description: Authorized terminal result, or uncertain when no terminal result is visible. An absent terminal result is never reported as confirmed failure.

503.description: Authorized lookup could not establish a terminal result. Proxies/network failures may provide no JSON at all; the client retains uncertainty locally.

get.summary: Look up a known operation ID in an authorized chapter
get.description: Read only. Reject query selectors. Resolve only inside the authorized chapter/record scope. A nonvisible ID does not prove absence or disclose an operation in another chapter.

get.description: Proposed exact wire; see x-chapter-context-contract. Restricted MFA states return safe 403 with no chapter/provider/authority disclosure. Every result no-store. Reject duplicate/unknown query selectors; X-Chapter-Context is the only selection-guard header. Header names are case insensitive. Missing/malformed guard is 400. Read choices with deterministic numeric ID order, limit 1..100 default 25, opaque user/epoch/limit-bound cursor; next_cursor null ends paging; no other filters.

chapterSession.name: ysp_session
chapterSession.description: Proposed cookie transport name for the session binding; final identity/session details are owned by the identity, record and evidence contract/P02. Must be Secure/HttpOnly and revalidated for current membership/duty/record visibility. Provider authority grants no chapter membership. Declaring this scheme does not implement authentication.

csrfToken.name: X-XSRF-TOKEN
csrfToken.description: URL-decode the XSRF-TOKEN cookie once and forward its encrypted opaque value unchanged. Required even for same-origin unsafe requests. Browser sends ysp_session automatically with credentials: include. No bearer or local-storage credential flow.

InvalidLookup.description: Invalid lookup selector after chapter authorization; no operation is executed.

AuthenticationRequired.description: Current authentication required. No stored operation or record details are returned.

ForbiddenLookup.description: Current chapter/duty/record authority does not permit lookup. No details are disclosed, including whether a supplied other-chapter ID exists.

UnavailableLookup.description: Authorized lookup could not establish a terminal result. Proxies/network failures may provide no JSON at all; the client retains uncertainty locally.

OperationCacheControl.description: Do not cache scoped operation results or uncertainty.

x-fingerprint-contract.identity: Enforce UNIQUE(chapter_id, action_code, idempotency_key), using case-sensitive action/key. The key identifies an attempt and is not an authority token.
x-fingerprint-contract.canonicalization: Validate against the owning input schema and reject duplicate JSON member names/unknown body fields before fingerprinting. Build {chapter_id, action_code, input_schema, input}; input contains all semantic request fields, exact record/line IDs, explicit expected_row_version and required expected_material_version, actual quantities/money and immutable evidence object/version/hash bindings. Normalize quantities/unit costs to six places and posted PHP to two with exact string/decimal arithmetic, never binary float. IDs remain strings, versions bounded integers, timestamps six-place UTC. Retain array order unless the owning schema explicitly declares set semantics. Distinguish omitted and null unless that schema explicitly normalizes them. Apply RFC 8785 JCS to the normalized value, encode UTF-8 without BOM and hash SHA-256. The server computes this; a client digest is untrusted.
x-fingerprint-contract.exclusions: Exclude the idempotency key itself, cookies, CSRF/attempt transport headers, trace metadata, request arrival time and expiring signed URLs. Include stable evidence bindings instead. Exclude no semantic field without an explicit owning-schema normalization. The attempted semantic input remains immutable while its result is uncertain.
x-fingerprint-contract.durability: Persist canonical fingerprint, unique chapter/action/key, terminal operation ID/result, business changes, audit and required durable follow-up in the same owning MySQL transaction. Source/action/batch uniqueness remains independently required. Same canonical payload replays the existing terminal ID/time after current authorization; changed payload under the same identity is rejected without replacing that result or adding an effect. A current authorization failure reveals no saved result. Terminal rejection may commit a result without a business posting; no terminal row means uncertain, not failed.

x-compatibility.agreement: Shared chapter/action/key, exact values, explicit row/material versions and uncertainty align with Q3?Q5. Quantity views, holds and posting/transaction ownership remain with the stock-hold and IPC/RM contracts and actual consumers; no future operation is accepted here.
Shared replay/current authority, exact PHP and separate progress/material meanings apply. Payment/coverage, release ownership and later endpoint payloads remain proposed.

Its proposed by-idempotency-key route maps to the chapter-scoped by-key selector with explicit action. Never accept key-only lookup. Source/recipient/batch/evidence payload and handover route remain proposed; no physical retry follows from database retry.

The newly present R-24 key-only /operations/{idempotencyKey} proposal requires action-aware adaptation to Q3 before use. by-id has a separate literal namespace to avoid mistaking a key for an operation ID. Its current_material_version maps explicitly to shared material_version; its richer chapter/actor/record envelope needs a reviewed adapter, not an assumed drop-in match. No RF endpoint or candidate status is promoted.

x-session-contract.authority: Codex contract proposal under owner-authorized session slice; not Glenn/Efren/security approval
x-session-contract.adapter: Proposed application-owned GET /csrf-cookie in Laravel web session/cookie stack; empty 204 response; EncryptCookies and shared MySQL session store. No Sanctum selected or installed.

forgery_policy.token: Mandatory X-XSRF-TOKEN on every unsafe P02 request, including same-origin; URL-decode readable encrypted XSRF-TOKEN cookie once, framework decrypts and compares to session token.
forgery_policy.origin: Additional application guard rejects Sec-Fetch-Site values other than same-origin when present and any supplied Origin not exactly equal to configured browser origin. If Fetch Metadata is absent, require exact Origin or same-origin Referer; otherwise 403 origin_forbidden. No same-site sibling allowance. HTTP loopback needs the same token/origin checks.
forgery_policy.framework_difference: Pinned PreventRequestForgery::handle uses hasValidOrigin OR tokensMatch. A dedicated adapter must enforce token AND origin; originOnly and the default middleware alone cannot satisfy this policy. Do not exempt unsafe routes. Reject _token and X-CSRF-TOKEN alternatives in the JSON adapter to avoid competing token precedence.
forgery_policy.same_origin_missing_token: 419 csrf_mismatch, even with valid credentials. It rejects this attempt only; an earlier uncertain attempt stays unresolved.

production.session_store: Shared MySQL; no replica-local session state

http_loopback.scope: Explicit local development profile only; localhost/127.0.0.1, never deployment
http_loopback.other_attributes: same names, host-only, Path=/, SameSite=Lax; session HttpOnly; same token/origin policy

cookies.rotation: Sign-in, successful MFA, privilege elevation and logout regenerate session ID and CSRF token. Logout invalidates old server session then issues fresh anonymous cookies; bootstrap revalidates disabled/revoked identity. GET /csrf-cookie reissues current CSRF token without unconditional rotation. Read current cookie immediately before each unsafe request; do not cache token in local storage.
cookies.lifetime: Numeric session/MFA lifetimes, attempt limits and recent-proof windows need subsequent security/backend approval. No fixture value approves a runtime default.

x-session-contract.consumer: Browser credentials: include; Accept: application/json; JSON Content-Type only with a JSON request body; redirect: error. Every result no-store. 204 has no body or Content-Type. No automatic unsafe retry after CSRF/429/network/protocol failure. Refresh/bootstrap can inform next action but never prove an earlier business attempt rejected.

Efren reviews restricted states, provider separation and Leader-authored access contract
Backend/security owner approves dedicated token AND origin adapter before affected contract freeze; numeric security values before runtime enablement
x-session-contract.deferred: The chapter-context slice extends AuthenticatedSession with chapter details; MFA slices own MFA operations. This slice implements no route, session persistence, authorization or screen.
x-session-contract.security_scheme_compatibility: Adopt ysp_session as the exact P02 session cookie spelling. Preserve the Stage 0 chapterSession scheme and lookup operations byte-semantically; its older proposed description is historical, with this extension supplying the current session details.

x-enrollment-contract.authority: Codex under owner-authorized enrollment slice; proposed wire contract, not peer/security approval
x-enrollment-contract.review_status: pending; affected contract freeze blocked on Glenn, Efren and backend/security review
x-enrollment-contract.binding: Current identity AND current server session own one live unconfirmed enrollment. Never accept caller user IDs. An enrollment identifier is distinct from an operation ID. Required MFA pending sessions can bootstrap, prepare/replace, confirm, refresh CSRF or sign out; no chapter/context, permissions or operational access.
x-enrollment-contract.preparation: POST /session/mfa/enrollment intent begin requires no live pending enrollment. intent replace_unconfirmed requires the matching live identifier and atomically invalidates its predecessor. Never replaces an already confirmed factor. Return setup URI/manual key only in this 200 response; no readback endpoint. A lost preparation response requires bootstrap and a reviewed next action; do not automatically begin or replace.
x-enrollment-contract.confirmation: POST /session/mfa/enrollment/confirm takes matching enrollment_id and authenticator_code. Validate expiry, session/identity binding and proof atomically before MFA becomes verified; consume enrollment and rotate session/CSRF. Only successful confirmation issues the initial one-time code set. Browser acknowledgment, copy or download is not proof and changes no authority. Repeat/consumed confirmation never reissues codes.
x-enrollment-contract.secrets: Passwords, OTPs, setup URI/manual key, enrollment material and recovery codes are transient; never editable drafts, local/session storage, IndexedDB, durable browser state, URL history, analytics or logs. Clear transient secret UI on completion/navigation/expiry/sign-out; recovery-code download is an explicit user-held secret export, never a browser draft. Bootstrap, errors, chapter context and normal reads cannot disclose setup material or recovery codes.
x-enrollment-contract.lost_confirmation: Never automatically repeat confirmation or restart enrollment. GET /session discovers current authentication only and never returns codes. See x-mfa-recovery-contract for explicit protected regeneration after bootstrap or safely blocked assisted recovery. A restricted snapshot does not establish rejection; no code delivery/readback is promised.
x-enrollment-contract.synthetic: All public fixtures, setup secrets, OTPs, codes, IDs, five-minute expiry, two-code example and Retry-After 30 are synthetic. Wire format/size bounds are not approved security limits. Actual MFA timing, code count/entropy, throttling/attempt values and proof policy require subsequent backend/security approval before runtime enablement.
x-enrollment-contract.scope: Schema and generated-consumer checks only. Binding, replacement invalidation, one-time verification/issuance, revocation, session rotation and pending-access denial are declarative server review obligations, not executed security enforcement. No production endpoints, code storage or UI.

x-mfa-recovery-contract.authority: Owner-authorized contract authoring; proposed wire behavior, not security/backend approval
x-mfa-recovery-contract.review_status: Glenn consumer, Efren domain/access and security/backend reviews pending; affected freeze/runtime gates remain
x-mfa-recovery-contract.challenge_binding: Sign-in and bootstrap return only restricted state with opaque challenge id and server expiry; never user, chapter, provider, duty or permission data. A challenge belongs to the current identity AND session. Bootstrap reports the current live challenge and never silently replaces it or extends expiry. Expired/consumed challenge with a remaining restricted session returns 409 on verify; bootstrap may report restricted state with expired metadata until reviewed sign-out/sign-in establishes a fresh challenge. No caller-selected account or challenge preparation endpoint.

regenerateRecoveryCodes: authenticated with mfa.status verified plus fresh password AND authenticator in this request

x-mfa-recovery-contract.verification: Select exactly one method and matching proof; reject mixed/extra fields. In one atomic transition validate current disabled status, current MFA policy and authority, session binding, live unconsumed challenge, expiry and factor; consume challenge and single-use recovery code (when chosen), establish verified MFA, rotate session/CSRF and recompute current session/authority. Concurrent attempts permit at most one success. A recovery proof never creates membership, duty, provider authority or a different identity. Authenticator replay/time policy is server-owned.
failure_precedence: challenge binding/live state or stale recent proof 409
x-mfa-recovery-contract.regeneration: Only explicit POST regeneration with both password and live authenticator proof in this request; no cached recent flag, recovery code substitute or retry-triggered generation. Validate freshness again at atomic commit using server-owned proof window. Replace the entire prior set atomically; old unused and consumed codes remain unusable. Issue new plaintext once on this 200, never on bootstrap, errors, list/read, challenge success or replay. Repeating is a new explicit protected replacement, never readback or idempotent replay. Restricted sessions must finish a challenge first.
x-mfa-recovery-contract.storage: Store recovery-code verifiers using protected one-way storage with secret-safe audit, atomic conditional consumption and whole-set replacement. Protect authenticator material at rest under restricted key access. Never log proof, passwords, setup secrets or plaintext codes. Transient consumer secrets are never editable drafts, durable browser state, URLs or analytics; clear on completion/navigation/expiry/logout. User-held export does not establish delivery or server readback.
x-mfa-recovery-contract.unknown_outcomes: Unknown challenge or confirmation response requires explicit GET bootstrap before any reviewed next step; no automatic retries. Authenticated verified state establishes current authentication only, never code delivery. Restricted state does not prove the previous mutation failed. Lost confirmation/regeneration issuance promises neither plaintext delivery nor readback nor automatic regeneration. After bootstrap, an officer retaining an authenticator can explicitly regenerate with fresh password and authenticator proof in a verified session; challenge-required officers first verify a factor. Loss of both usable factors reaches only the blocked assisted-recovery guidance. Logout always remains available.
x-mfa-recovery-contract.assisted_recovery: Read-only stable unavailable/blocker response; only bootstrap_session and sign_out navigation. No reset authority, identity-proof upload, contact, email/SMS, support ticket, notification or reset operation is authorized. Restoring identity would never add chapter authority.
x-mfa-recovery-contract.server_values: Challenge lifetime, session lifetime, attempt limits, authenticator replay/time policy, recent password/authenticator proof window and code entropy/count require subsequent security/backend approval before runtime enablement. All fixture IDs, proofs, code count, UTC dates and Retry-After are public synthetic examples, never prototype defaults.
x-mfa-recovery-contract.validation_boundary: Executed schema/example validation, deterministic generation, strict positive/negative compile checks and synthetic consumer exchanges only. Scenarios marked declarative_server_review are obligations for future real backend security/concurrency/storage/revocation tests, not executed security evidence.

x-chapter-context-contract.review_status: Glenn consumer and Efren domain/access review pending; exact concurrency fields/header and authority matrix are explicit affected-freeze blockers until reviewed.
x-chapter-context-contract.session_reuse: Chapter results wrap the canonical AuthenticatedSession without changing SessionSnapshot, sign-in or MFA success. Restricted states cannot access any chapter operation; 403 is closed safe feedback with no identity, choices, provider, context or permissions. Use GET /session to discover required MFA; signed out/expired/disabled is 401. Session/CSRF policy remains x-session-contract.

chapter_states.no_authorized_memberships: Successful empty context, including provider-only navigation. Provider destinations remain in the canonical authenticated session. No context or fabricated chapter is returned.
chapter_states.selection_required: Multiple current authorized memberships and no valid restored selection; explicit select required. Never pick the first list item automatically.
chapter_states.selected: One authorized membership may be selected directly after required MFA, disclosed as sole_membership. A still-current restored selection is disclosed as restored, including when many memberships exist. Explicit selection reports explicit. Every selected response identifies the checked user/chapter/membership tuple; compare membership.chapter_id/name/id to context and requested scope.

choices.order: Ascending numeric chapter_id then membership_id, using exact unsigned decimal comparison, never lexical or floating point. One current membership per user/chapter. Canonical ChapterMembershipChoice is used identically in selected read and list.
choices.pagination: Optional single-valued limit integer 1..100 (default 25), cursor opaque cur_ token. next_cursor null means end, including a successful empty page. Non-null means another page. Items <= returned limit; each page reauthorizes and never fills from a stale authority snapshot. Not a stable cross-page snapshot; membership changes may omit items or shorten pages; refresh from first page to reconcile. Tokens bind current user, authorization epoch, ordering and initial limit; invalid/expired/wrong-user/changed-limit cursor gets safe 400 invalid_selector. Never encode trusted identity from caller.
choices.filters: Only current authenticated user active authorized memberships; no caller user/chapter/duty/search/status filter. Inactive/disabled/revoked excluded. No query aliases, duplicates, arrays, numeric chapter IDs, empty cursor, unknown fields or competing body/query selectors; reject 400 before selection. Valid unknown and unauthorized chapter selections both return identical safe 403.
choices.canonical_version: membership_version is the positive membership authority revision, mapped to memberships.authority_version. Grant authorization/revoke/disable changes increment it atomically; effective time is independently rechecked even without a new stored revision.

x-chapter-context-contract.mfa: Server computes MFA need from ALL currently effective approver/admin grants and provider administration before any protected access or chapter disclosure. Selected duty, current chapter and client mfa flag never reduce this requirement. New privilege, grant expiry/revocation and account changes trigger next-access reevaluation, independently of a client revision. No choice list before required MFA. Provider administration also requires MFA without an operational chapter. Not-required requester fixtures have no privileged effective authority anywhere.

internal_compatibility.projection: ChapterDuty/ChapterDutyGrant and ChapterCurrentContext project existing definitions with shared exact IDs/versions/UTC. Only available_actions is narrowed to this finite P02 chapter catalogue. Tests validate both selected context examples with the unchanged internal schema and preserve each projected property. No new session union fields or internal boolean reinterpretation.

mfa_examples.meaning: Current required MFA verified; check-time reevaluation still required.
Current MFA gate satisfied because this identity currently needs no MFA; does not assert a factor was verified.

internal_compatibility.policy_and_attribution: Action execution resolves current approved chapter PolicyReference (exact policy version/material approval/settings hash and effective dates), never a client approved flag. Preserve immutable Attribution using actual user/membership/duty grant/code, names and capture time even after disable. Context/navigation does not disclose policy material or fabricate approval references. Policy/status operations and record attribution belong to later slices/providers.

action_authority.catalogue: ./p02-action-catalogue.json; P02Action finite union, P02ChapterAction excludes provider/global actions. Three separate provider authorities remain provisioner, billing_admin, recovery_operator. All fourteen canonical duties are represented; duties absent from an action row grant none of that action.
action_authority.matrix_semantics: Rows are candidate maximum eligibility, never permission by themselves. Evaluate scope, effective grant/alternate/limits, required MFA, current policy, material/row versions, readiness, stage, entitlement and actual-identity independence for EACH operation. Sensitive read, preparation, approval, revoke and disable are distinct. Navigation, sole membership and union of visible actions grant no general access; no wildcard role. Safe blockers may be returned without sensitive settings.
action_authority.ownership: Chapter Head authorizes chapter memberships/duties/alternates and operational settings only. Finance approves financial settings. Preparation is distinct from authorization; counter/Inventory/sales/requester duties do not imply Finance/Head. Unsupported setting variants remain unwritable/unapprovable until the minimum-policy slice.
action_authority.provider: Provider catalogue entries never appear in chapter available_actions. Provisioner can only use separately authorized organization-bound provisioning/initial appointment/identity-reference procedures; billing_admin/recovery_operator have no enabled P02 action by inference. A provider with separately approved membership gets only that membership duties. identity.disable has no authorized duty/provider and enabled_boundary false pending separately approved global procedure (global-disable slice). Catalogue entries do not implement later endpoints.
action_authority.independence: Compare actual immutable user identities and participation, not duty labels. Own-RF/purchase/ordinary ADJ/count variance/booth conflicts follow GOV-05-GOV-07/TR-17 Appendix D. Head+Finance variance requires at least two eligible people, neither preparer nor affected custodian; overlapping duties need approved independent fallback. There is no global actor_id != preparer_id rule: authorized receiving preparer may post inspected RM with valid source/evidence/duplicate checks.

concurrency.fields: selection_revision: opaque ctx_ token, server bound to current session selection epoch; distinct from context.authority_version (positive bounded integer), membership.membership_version, and owning row/material versions. Never order opaque tokens or use timestamp as a version.
concurrency.selection_guard: POST selectChapter requires X-Chapter-Context with the exact last successful ChapterSnapshot.selection_revision plus chapter_id, membership_id and expected_membership_version. No actor/duty/approved/context in the body. Compare revision, current session/MFA, target authorization/tuple and membership version atomically; commit selection with a new revision. A same-target explicit reselect still advances revision. No Idempotency-Key, durable result, or replay for this navigation transition.
concurrency.stale: 409 chapter_context_stale with only message and next_action refresh_context. No replacement revision, chapter or policy is disclosed on errors. Known rejection changes no selection. GET context after invalidated/revoked selection first reports safe 409 while clearing it and advancing revision; next GET reports recomputed empty/required/sole state. Unauthorized/nonexistent target is identical 403; when both stale revision and invalid target occur, current revision is checked first, without target existence disclosure. After scope assertion mismatch return 409 without changing a valid current selection.
concurrency.protected_mutation_boundary: Future selected-context chapter mutations must carry X-Chapter-Context and owning expected_authority_version, row/material versions as specified by their operation. Before dispatch and again at commit, atomically bind selected chapter/tuple/revision to route/body scope and current authority. Context revision only guards switching; expiry/disable/policy/effective grant changes independently invalidate authorization even with unchanged revision. Exact per-operation mutation bodies are authored in later administration slices, not a generic arbitrary payload endpoint.
concurrency.prepared_mutation: An unfinished command pins original chapter_id, action_code, exact semantic payload, input schema, expected authority/row/material versions, selection revision and original chapter/action/idempotency key. Switching never relabels/reposts it. Stale response requires refresh AND explicit original-scope review; never replace pinned values or automatically resend. Same retained attempt can be investigated only against its original chapter; new reviewed intent needs its own attempt.
concurrency.original_lookup: Existing chapter-scoped by-key/by-id operations retain exact Stage 0 schemas. After switching to chapter 2, lookup for original chapter 1 stays scoped to 1 and reauthorizes the original action/identity against CURRENT authority for 1, not the active selection. No selected-context header required for lookup; switching alone grants no access. Revocation returns safe forbidden with no saved result; uncertainty remains. Nonchapter durable scopes wait for the provisioning/global-disable slices.
concurrency.unknown_selection: Lost response: explicitly bootstrap/current-context read to learn current navigation; no automatic select retry. Current state does not establish success of an earlier business mutation. No automatic request after transport/protocol/CSRF/throttle/stale failure.

x-chapter-context-contract.enforcement: HTTP commands and queries, background jobs at execution, and every protected file/PDF/CSV/download at delivery independently recheck current identity, chapter membership, effective grants, MFA, policy, scope, independence, stage and entitlement. A queued job/export never inherits authority from preparation. Disable/revoke removes future access while historical attribution remains immutable.
x-chapter-context-contract.validation_boundary: JSON schema enforces shapes, finite duties/actions, closed discriminants, exact IDs/UTC/versions, bounds and no fields on safe errors. Relationship, token binding, pagination ordering, MFA applicability, nonenumeration, concurrency, authority and independent-person rules are declarative_server_review scenarios; synthetic consumer exchanges are not backend/security enforcement. Runtime-only constraints include regex/range/array uniqueness/size/oneOf relationships; generated types alone do not prove them.

x-membership-contract.identity_lookup: POST exact canonical existing user_id only, behind current Chapter Head memberships.prepare permission and MFA. No prefix/name/email search, pagination, public registration or credentials. Nonexistent, disabled, ineligible and nonvisible identities return identical 200 identity:null, with no reason. Uniform safe messages and rate limits; timing/nonenumeration enforcement remains P03/runtime work. This proposal cannot freeze before reviewer approval.
x-membership-contract.authorization: Server binds actor from session and current Chapter Head action permission in original chapter. Recheck MFA and current grants on every read, mutation, replay, lookup, job and protected delivery. Provider authority alone grants nothing. Read/list memberships.read; identity lookup memberships.prepare; mutation action is exact memberships.authorize/disable/revoke. Browser fields and navigation are not authority.
x-membership-contract.pagination: GET memberships accepts optional status, limit default 50 (1..100), cursor. Order immutable membership_id numeric ascending (decimal comparison, never JS Number). next_cursor null ends; nonnull means another page. Opaque server cursor binds actor, chapter, status, limit and snapshot; invalid/expired/mismatched cursor is 400, never restarts silently. Membership changes invalidate snapshot: 409 review original query. Empty list is success. No global query. IDs uniquely identify items.
x-membership-contract.attempt: Pin original chapter, action, idempotency key, X-Chapter-Context revision, expected actor authority version and target resource version (including explicit null absence). Freeze canonical payload bytes and SHA-256 fingerprint server-side: RFC 8785 canonical JSON of {chapter_id,action_code,membership_id,context_revision,body} (membership_id null only for authorize; exact path target for disable/revoke); body includes original key and version fields. Do not accept a client fingerprint. Original identity is actor-session bound. Unique chapter/action/key is atomic with resource changes, result, audit and follow-up under P03.
x-membership-contract.replay: Recheck current access first. Compare immutable fingerprint before stale guard evaluation for an existing terminal same-key attempt: authorized identical replay returns original membership/version, operation ID and committed_at with replayed:true, even if original versions are now stale. Never execute again. Different payload under original key -> 409 idempotency_conflict. Different action/chapter/key is a distinct attempt, never recovery; do not offer a new key while original outcome is unknown. For a new attempt, stale context/authority/resource -> distinct 409 codes; no side effect. Missing versions/client actor/authority/approved flags -> 422; bad selectors/headers -> 400. 401/403/419 cannot establish earlier failure.
x-membership-contract.lookup_compatibility: Both old lookup forms and record branches preserved byte-for-byte in shared definitions. Added MembershipLookupTerminal to HTTP 200 union is additive on wire but incompatible with exhaustive old consumers that assume every terminal has record; consumers must discriminate resource_type before old action_result handling. No old required field, enum or nullability changed. Membership pending/not-visible and unavailable reuse LookupPending/LookupUnavailable without fabricated record, using null record and unknown operation; HTTP 200 alone is not commitment. Actual consumer approval remains a freeze blocker.
x-membership-contract.lifecycle: Disable/revoke ends only this chapter membership immediately; retains identity, all historical attribution and independently authorized other memberships. Reauthorization requires exact retained version. Never deletes global identity or infers global disable authority (separate later boundary). New protected operations and queued jobs/delivery must recheck current scope; cancel/suppress protected output after revocation, preserve durable business outcome and audit, do not roll back completed work. Atomic persistence, crash recovery and outbox are P03, synthetic fixtures only.
x-membership-contract.feedback: FieldFeedback RFC 6901 pointers are relative to actual request body. Codes/messages are safe; no candidate secrets. Correct non-secret edits remain separate from immutable attempt. Logout/session interruption/revocation conceals protected edits; resume only same identity after current authorization and version review. Chapter switch never retargets original attempt. No secret retention, offline synchronization or reload persistence promised. Timeout, malformed JSON/HTML/redirect or lost connection leaves original outcome uncertain; never auto-replay or fabricate failed outcome.
x-membership-contract.terminal_rejection: P03 may durably record an atomic membership state rejection: 409 MembershipRejected without fabricated resulting membership/record. Original ID and terminal transaction time survive authorized replay/lookup (HTTP 200 MembershipLookupRejected, replayed:true). Predurable field/guard/access failures have no operation and cannot establish an earlier attempt outcome.

x-duty-grant-contract.review_status: Proposed P02 wire; freeze blockers: actual Glenn consumer, Efren domain/access and security review of grant scope, limit meaning, alternates, effective history and replay. Synthetic values approve no officers or limits.
x-duty-grant-contract.authorization: Every operation requires current authenticated membership in path chapter, MFA and exact Chapter Head action from p02-action-catalogue.json; provider roles and buyers are not duties. Catalogue/list/read use duty_grants.read. Authorize uses duty_grants.authorize; amend uses duty_grants.prepare; end/revoke use duty_grants.revoke; substitute uses alternates.authorize. Request fields are never authority. Newly effective admin authority re-evaluates MFA.
x-duty-grant-contract.visibility: Only current authorized Chapter Head sees catalogue and grant details, minimal canonical existing identity and version/history metadata; lists/read share AdminDutyGrant. Unknown, other-chapter, inaccessible grants/memberships/units or alternate references yield the same 404 duty_grant_not_visible, no leaked current versions. Denied operation itself yields 403 without protected fields. Current versions appear only under authorized visibility. Current context refresh and read give versions for a fresh reviewed attempt; stale replies do not disclose them.
x-duty-grant-contract.pagination: Catalogue is the complete fixed fourteen codes ordered lexicographically by duty_code, no pagination or filters applicable and no editable role/permission API. Grant list accepts membership_id, duty_code, scope_kind, requesting_unit_id, status (effective/scheduled/ended/revoked), limit default 50 bounded 1..100, cursor; no other filters. Unit selector requires scope_kind=unit. All filters conjunctive, status evaluated at snapshot UTC. Order immutable grant id numeric ascending by decimal comparison, never JS Number. next_cursor null is end; nonnull indicates a remaining page. Empty succeeds. Opaque cursor binds actor, chapter, exact normalized filters, limit and snapshot; invalid/expired/mismatched ->400; changed snapshot ->409 grant_stale, no silent restart. No global enumeration.
x-duty-grant-contract.intervals: starts_at inclusive, ends_at exclusive; null open end. Server rejects reversed/empty intervals and new backdated changes. Amend cannot change membership/duty/scope, rewrite prior effective history or undo revocation. End may shorten/schedule only; revoke immediate server commit. Same-membership/same-duty/same-scope overlapping unrevoked grants conflict; adjacent intervals allowed; distinct duties may overlap. Chapter and unit are different scopes, but applicable policy still limits actions.
x-duty-grant-contract.limits: DutyGrantTerms is canonical. PHP exact per-action cap, null gives no monetary authority from this grant; no unlimited sentinel. Zero cap permits only zero value. Policy may impose narrower authority. Head authorization does not imply Finance policy approval. Limit increases or alternate limits outside independently approved assigning authority return 403; no client approved flag.
x-duty-grant-contract.substitution: Atomic original end plus new alternate grant; same chapter, duty and scope, different immutable user identity and authorized target membership. Version-check original grant and both memberships plus actor authority/context. Same user in another role cannot supply independence. Original authorized attribution and all historical events remain. New alternate records replaces_grant_id; original ends at new start; alternate expiration never resurrects original. No automatic self-approval or automatic promotion.
x-duty-grant-contract.independence: GOV-05-GOV-07 checks use immutable users.id for the specific decision. Own RF approval, own Inventory purchase commitment and sole ordinary ADJ approval blocked; count preparer/affected custodian cannot approve variance at all. Head/Finance variance approvals need two distinct eligible people, preserving both duty decisions with independent fallback or approved alternate; no preparer/custodian fallback. Booth own close-out needs another reviewer; overlapping sales/collection/verification needs independent review. Authorized receiving officer may prepare and post inspected RM after source/evidence checks; no blanket ban on every later preparer action. Role switching creates no independent person.
x-duty-grant-contract.attempt: Reuse x-membership-contract canonical attempt/result/feedback conventions. Server fingerprint RFC 8785 canonical JSON {chapter_id,action_code,grant_id,context_revision,body}; grant_id null only authorize, exact path id otherwise. body includes target membership, full submitted terms, reason, key and all versions. Authenticated actor bound server-side. Atomic original chapter/action/key uniqueness and immutable fingerprint; changed body or target under same key ->409 idempotency_conflict. End and revoke share duty_grants.revoke so differing command body distinguishes them. Never accept a client fingerprint or attribution.
x-duty-grant-contract.replay: Recheck current original-scope access first; identical authorized terminal replay returns original operation ID, commit time and resulting snapshots/versions with replayed:true before evaluating new-attempt stale guards. No second effect or new history. Different context/payload under old key conflicts. Stale chapter_context/authority/membership/grant ->distinct 409 without mutation for new attempts. Missing guard/invalid shapes ->422; malformed parameters ->400. Reauthentication cannot restore expired/revoked authority.
x-duty-grant-contract.outcomes: Success has duty_grant resource, resulting grant and nullable replaced_grant (nonnull only substitution), resulting versions and durable operation. Both original lookup selectors add DutyGrantLookupTerminal/Rejected, preserving old record/membership branches. Original scope and current authorization remain mandatory for lookup. Additive wire union is a source compatibility change for exhaustive consumers; discriminate resource_type. Durable rejection has rejected operation and safe duty_grant_state_conflict, no fake grant/record. HTTP200 pending and 503 unavailable remain uncertainty, never proof of failure; no automatic unsafe retry or new key while unresolved.
x-duty-grant-contract.lifecycle: End/revoke/substitution removes only grant authority at its effective boundary; membership, global identity, other grants and other chapters remain independently authorized. Membership disable/revoke instead removes all authority from that membership. Preserve original actor attribution, effective grant history and durable results. Every protected action, replay/lookup, queued job, export and delivery rechecks effective interval, revocation, membership, immutable individual independence, MFA, approved scope and limits; suppress now-unauthorized protected output without erasing a prior committed result.
x-duty-grant-contract.feedback: Reuse MembershipInvalid and FieldFeedback RFC6901 paths relative to actual body, e.g. /grant/ends_at. Keep correct nonsecret edits separate from frozen original attempt; interruption conceals edits and resume needs same identity, current access and version review. Chapter switching never retargets attempt; timeout/lost connection/HTML/malformed/redirect does not establish failure. No secret/offline/reload persistence promised.
x-duty-grant-contract.server_checks: JSON Schema validates closed structures, exact IDs/times/money, required versions and scope/reference compatibility. Interval comparisons, duplicate overlap, same-chapter and same-duty alternate relationships, authority/limit approval, two-person independence, atomic fingerprint/replay/history, cursor binding/order and revocation/queued output require future P03/server checks. No runtime enforcement, persistence or human acceptance is established.
